# SOOS — CAP Regulation Record Schema (CAP-RRS)
# draft-sato-soos-cap-rrs-03
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/cap-rrs/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: September 5, 2026

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

CAP-RRS is the compiler that translates human-readable legal obligations into machine-executable Cedar policies, and the schema for the Regulation Record artifact that carries a legal obligation's provenance end to end. CAP owns runtime enforcement of the compiled policies; CAP-RRS owns regulation-to-policy translation, versioning, certification, and the law-changed/interpretation-changed lifecycle. The compile() function and Constitutional Mandate Registry (CMR) belong to CAP-RRS, not CAP. CAP-RRS also owns the Tier 3 resource-policy escalation classes (HEM_TIER3_ANTICIPATORY / HEM_TIER3_OBSERVED) that CAP defers to it.

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

Without CAP-RRS, your CAP-governed deployment has no standardized way to:

- Translate regulations into Cedar policies without custom engineering per jurisdiction per regulation — the Regulation Record schema and Cedar Compilation Profile make encoded regulations composable, and the Constitutional Mandate Registry (CMR) distributes them as signed, versioned packages
- Prove which statutory version a loaded Cedar policy was certified against, and keep that provenance current when the law changes — the Law Reference Interface (LRI) generic model (Japan e-LAWS, EU ELI, US USLM profiles) and the Statute-Primacy Rule specify exactly this
- Detect a statutory amendment or a superseding interpretation, suspend the affected Cedar policy, and resolve it without ever mutating the GAR record that logged the original conflict — the CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT / INTERPRETATION_SUPERSEDED event pair and their *_RESOLVED counterparts specify this append-only
- Handle the Tier 3 resource and usage policy lifecycle — HEM_TIER3_ANTICIPATORY (pre-mission) and HEM_TIER3_OBSERVED (mid-mission) escalation, the Execution Options Package, and Natural Breakpoint Declaration are specified in CAP-RRS, not CAP
- Certify who may sign a Regulation Record at what tier, and verify that signature before a GEC will load it — the five-tier Certification Model (FOUNDATION / REGULATORY_BODY / LICENSED_PROVIDER / OPERATOR / SELF)

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

These terms are normative in CAP-RRS-03 and must not be paraphrased away:

Regulation Record:
   The JSON artifact that encodes a legal obligation as a CAP-tiered Cedar policy source. Top-level fields include: record_id (format {publisher_id}.{instrument_code}.{article}), schema_version, tier ("0-A"/"0-B"/"1"/"2"/"3"), jurisdiction_scope (territories, legal_system, supranational_body), legal_source (instrument_name, instrument_code, article, official_url; treaty_citation REQUIRED for Tier 0-A), title, operative_clause, agent_check (trigger + prohibition_condition/permission_condition + required_context_fields + post_deny_protocol), conflict_declarations, certification (certification_tier, certified_by, certification_date, certification_statement, record_signature, certification_expiry), effective_date, sunset_date, review_trigger, record_version (semver), supersedes, and — REQUIRED as of -02 — authority_source_uri.

Cedar Compilation Profile:
   The normative specification for compiling Regulation Records into Cedar. Compiles in tier order (0-A, 0-B, 1, 2, 3; lexicographic by record_id within a tier). Maps agent_check.prohibition_condition to a Cedar forbid clause and permission_condition to a Cedar permit clause; annotates every compiled policy with record_id, tier, jurisdiction_scope.territories, effective_date, and record_version so the GEC can produce structured DENY reason codes. A conforming compiler MUST reject records with invalid/expired certification and MUST NOT compile a record past its sunset_date.

Constitutional Mandate Registry (CMR):
   The signed package ecosystem Regulation Records are distributed through. A package (cmr://{publisher}.{instrument}@{version}) bundles records, a changelog, declared conflicts, and an Ed25519 package_signature, versioned per Semantic Versioning: MAJOR (an operative clause tightened — operator review REQUIRED), MINOR (new clauses added — review RECOMMENDED), PATCH (metadata only — automatic upgrade PERMITTED). GECs subscribe to signed Update Notifications and respond ACCEPT / REVIEW_AND_APPROVE / PIN. Every distributed update as of -02 carries a catalog_version object (Section 10.5).

compile():
   cap.compile() resolves conflict_declarations, applies the Cedar Compilation Profile, and produces a signed, versioned Cedar policy set the GEC loads. Developer workflow: cap.import("cmr://...") per regulation dependency, cap.operator_policy()/cap.resource_policy() for Tier 2/3, then compile() — no Cedar authored by hand except for debugging.

Certification Model:
   Five publisher tiers, each scoped to specific CAP tiers: FOUNDATION (ATP Foundation; Tier 0-A/0-B only, certified against treaty text), REGULATORY_BODY (national/supranational authority; Tier 1 within statutory jurisdiction), LICENSED_PROVIDER (third party licensed by a regulatory body; Tier 1 within license scope), OPERATOR (the deploying org; Tier 2, no external approval), SELF (developer/operator; Tier 3, no external approval). Publishers register an Ed25519 keypair with the CMR; FOUNDATION and REGULATORY_BODY publishers undergo identity verification. A GEC MUST verify registration currency, signature, certification_expiry, and tier-consistency before loading any package.

Conflict Declaration Model:
   How the compiler surfaces contradictory Regulation Records. Static conflicts (same action_scope, structurally contradictory conditions) MUST be caught at compile time. Runtime conflicts (only certain Cedar context combinations trigger both policies) are surfaced as HEM_JURISDICTIONAL_CONFLICT (Class 5) annotations the GEC evaluates live. A conflict_declaration with strategy OPERATOR_DECLARES_PRIORITY blocks compilation until the operator signs a resolution declaration (resolution_id, the two record_ids, resolution, legal_basis, authorized_by) that is itself stored in the GAR audit record.

Law Reference Interface (LRI) [NEW in -02]:
   The jurisdiction-neutral schema (authority_source block: law_id, article_ref, version_identifier, retrieved_at, amendment_detection_endpoint, interpretation_endpoint, endorsement) that gives a Regulation Record machine-readable provenance back to living statutory text. Three profiles are defined: Japan (e-LAWS), EU (ELI), US (USLM) — the same relationship OSCAL profiles (NIST 800-53, ISO 27001) have to the underlying OSCAL catalog format. The endorsement block's resolution_basis field records the legal character of the endorsement: statute_clear, interpretive_ruling (REQUIRES resolution_instrument_id), internal_conflict_resolution, or cross_statute_coordination (REQUIRES co_endorsement_required/co_endorsers).

Statute-Primacy Rule [NEW in -02]:
   A Cedar policy never overrides a statute. When amendment_detection_endpoint (polled <=24h) surfaces an amendment posterior to endorsed_at, the GEC MUST raise CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT, provisionally suspend the Cedar policy for new actions, and escalate to HEM — the session stays open, in-progress actions already PERMITted are protected by the Safe Harbor Clause. An interpretive (not textual) change fires the parallel INTERPRETATION_SUPERSEDED event via interpretation_endpoint instead, routing to the authority that issued the superseded ruling rather than the primary statutory authority.

CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT_RESOLVED / INTERPRETATION_SUPERSEDED_RESOLVED [NEW in -03]:
   Resolution (re-endorsement or human override) of either conflict type is now its own GAR event, carrying resolves_event_id back to the original conflict entry's entry_id, resolved_at, resolved_by, new_endorsed_at, and rationale (REQUIRED for human_override). The original conflict event is never modified. -02's schema instead populated a "resolution" field on the original entry after the fact — an in-place mutation of an already-committed, potentially SCITT-anchored GAR record. -03 fixes this at its actual origin: the same mutation pattern had already been independently caught and fixed downstream, in GAR's own ALE-NEW-03 (Section 12.17(c)) and in CAP's Section 8.9.4 Phase 4 step (5), before being traced back to this document as the schema's root cause.

Tier 3 / HEM Integration:
   HEM_TIER3_ANTICIPATORY (Class 8) fires pre-mission when estimated cost exceeds remaining budget under a policy with anticipatory_assessment: true — execution halts before any step begins. HEM_TIER3_OBSERVED (Class 9) fires mid-mission at warning_threshold_pct — execution does NOT halt immediately; the GEC commits to completing the next Natural Breakpoint first. Both classes construct an Execution Options Package (full_mission_viable, budget figures, an array of natural_breakpoints each with cost/viability/value_delivered, an array of recourse_options — SCOPE_REDUCTION / COMMERCIAL_UPGRADE / TEMPORAL_DEFERRAL — and a recommended_option) for the human decision. Agents under a policy with natural_breakpoint_required: true MUST declare their Natural Breakpoints before beginning multi-step execution.

---

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

OSCAL (Open Security Controls Assessment Language):
   OSCAL makes regulations machine-readable; CAP makes them machine-enforceable. CAP-RRS is the bridge, consuming OSCAL-formatted control records as input to the Cedar Compilation Profile. The LRI Profile model (Section 9) is explicitly the same pattern as OSCAL profiles: e-LAWS, ELI, and USLM are LRI profiles of one underlying LRI schema, the way NIST 800-53 and ISO 27001 are OSCAL profiles of one underlying OSCAL catalog format.

SCITT (Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency and Trust):
   The Constitutional Mandate Registry applies SCITT transparency-log principles to legal records: the statute is the claim, the certifying publisher is the SCITT issuer, and CMR registration carries a SCITT inclusion proof. This is why -03's fix to make conflict resolution append-only (rather than mutating a committed entry) matters — an entry anchored under a SCITT inclusion proof cannot honestly be edited afterward.

Cedar (AWS — Apache 2.0):
   Cedar is the policy language CAP-RRS compiles to and CAP's CEE evaluates. CAP-RRS does not define Cedar semantics — it defines the normative mapping (Cedar Compilation Profile) from Regulation Records to Cedar policies, tier-ordered and annotated for GEC reason-code production.

EU AI Act Article 5, GDPR Article 22:
   Both require that automated decisions be explainable/disclosable. CAP's PTD framework (CAP-05 Section 12a) satisfies this at the kernel level; CAP-RRS Regulation Records are the structured record PTD discloses from, at SUMMARY or FULL level via ptd_endpoint.

---

## SECTION 5 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

This draft depends on:
   CAP (draft-sato-soos-cap-05) — CAP defines the CEE that evaluates the Cedar policies CAP-RRS compiles; Tier 3 resource/usage policy enforcement in CAP requires CAP-RRS; CAP Section 8.9.4's catalog-conflict resolution fix was itself propagated from this document's -03 schema correction.
   HEM (draft-sato-soos-hem-06) — Tier 3 Class 8 (HEM_TIER3_ANTICIPATORY) and Class 9 (HEM_TIER3_OBSERVED) escalation, and the general CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT / INTERPRETATION_SUPERSEDED HEM escalation path, are both CAP-RRS-defined HEM interaction classes.

The following drafts depend on this draft:
   CAP (draft-sato-soos-cap-05) — normatively coupled; implementing CAP Tier 3 requires CAP-RRS; compile() is normatively defined here and referenced there.
   GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-07) — CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT, CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT_RESOLVED, INTERPRETATION_SUPERSEDED, and INTERPRETATION_SUPERSEDED_RESOLVED are all registered in the GAR ALE registry; the compiled Cedar policy set's hash is recorded in the GEC Manifest.
   KIA (draft-sato-soos-kia-06) — the GEC Manifest includes the hash of the compiled Cedar policy set produced by CAP-RRS compile(); a Manifest mismatch invalidates the KIA attestation.

## SECTION 6 — Datatracker Status

Draft identifier: draft-sato-soos-cap-rrs-03
Submission date: September 5, 2026
Current version: -03
Status: Active Individual Submission, IETF Datatracker
Datatracker: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-sato-soos-cap-rrs/
Draft page: https://soosproject.ai/drafts/cap-rrs
Root llms.txt: https://soosproject.ai/llms.txt

What -02 and -03 actually changed:
   -02 added three new sections (Law Reference Interface, Statute-Primacy Rule, Operational Requirements) but, per -03's own changelog, shipped Sections 5 through 8 (Cedar Compilation Profile, Conflict Declaration Model, Certification Model, CMR Protocol) as bracket placeholders with no body text. -03 reconstructs all four sections from the original -01 text (unchanged in substance) and fixes the Statute-Primacy Rule's event schemas at their root: catalog-conflict resolution is now a new, causally-linked GAR event (CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT_RESOLVED / INTERPRETATION_SUPERSEDED_RESOLVED) rather than a mutation of the original conflict entry.

Relevant IETF communities:
   No existing IETF WG owns regulation-to-policy compilation for AI systems. CAP-RRS is positioned as a gap-filling Individual Submission. Relevant communities: SAAG (security area), PEARG (privacy regulation encoding), SCITT (the CMR's transparency-log model and the -03 append-only fix), OSCAL Foundation and NIST OSCAL team (OSCAL-to-LRI bridge).

Open questions (Section 13):
   OQ-CAP-PATTERN (pattern-before-threshold), OQ-CAP-XJURIS (cross-jurisdiction Tier 1 compilation — runtime jurisdiction-selection algorithm not yet specified), JP-OQ-03/JP-OQ-04 (Japan interpretation registry — e-LAWS API v2 does not yet expose interpretive instruments; formal spec deferred to draft-sato-soos-cap-rrs-jp-00), JP-OQ-01 (co-endorsement authority for cross-prefectural rules — individual governors vs. National Governors' Association).
